title: Certify the Barker/circulant-Hadamard classification in reference works (Wikipedia, OEIS, MathWorld, MATLAB docs)
summary: The circulant Hadamard theorem (orders 1 and 4 only) is Lean-checked against a comparator statement using only the three standard axioms, and it closes the even-length Barker case, which was the only open case. Together with Turyn-Storer and Schmidt-Willms (odd lengths, peer-reviewed), binary Barker sequences of length n>1 exist exactly for n in {2,3,4,5,7,11,13}. As of Oct 2026, Wikipedia (Barker code, Hadamard matrix), OEIS A091704, MathWorld and MATLAB docs still say 'conjectured', 'open' or 'maximum known'.

beneficiaries: Radar/sonar/spread-spectrum engineers and students reading reference material; sequence-design researchers who would otherwise spend effort on even-length Barker searches
first_step: Edit the Wikipedia 'Barker code' Conjecture section to say the even case follows from the circulant Hadamard theorem (OpenAI preprint, Sept 2026, with a Lean proof), while flagging that the paper is a non-peer-reviewed preprint. Also submit an OEIS A091704 comment edit and re-tag the formal-conjectures Barker statement 'solved' with a link to the Lean proof.
measurement: Number of reference pages updated, and whether editors accept a Lean-verified preprint as a source. Wikipedia's reliable-source policy may require peer-reviewed publication first.
risks: Citation politics: Wikipedia and OEIS editors may hold out for journal publication. Five earlier complete proofs had been claimed (2016-2025) without acceptance, so caution is reasonable even with Lean, since Lean checks the statement as formalized and the comparator statement must be read. The engineering decision is unchanged, because nobody has designed a system expecting a Barker code longer than 13 since 1961.

title: Upstream circulant-Hadamard + even-Barker proof to Mathlib (Archive first)
summary: The proof is about 9.5k lines in 68 files, plus about 280 lines in 5 files for Barker. It depends only on Mathlib plus OAI-internal files (no other OAI library, no sorry, no native_decide), on pinned Mathlib d13f23b and Lean v4.34.1. Mathlib already has Matrix.circulant, Matrix.IsHadamard (2026) with four_dvd_card, and Kronecker's theorem NumberField.Embeddings.pow_eq_one_of_norm_eq_one, so the bridge statements are small. The bulk (cyclic group-ring, cyclotomic localizations, alternating character products) is reusable algebraic number theory, but it is written as a monolithic proof and not in Mathlib style.

title: Retire 'bounded / Golay 12.32' framing in LABS, QAOA-benchmark and survey texts
summary: Corollary cor:merit, a Lean-checked consequence via m_N->1 and F >= 1/(m_N^2-1), shows that the maximum binary merit factor tends to infinity through all N. This disproves Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture, so Golay's 12.32 cannot be the asymptotic optimum. Current LABS and quantum papers still describe 12.32 as the conjectured or 'proposed' asymptotic limit, or say the merit factor 'should stay approximately constant'. Only a wording change is needed, since no finite-N claim is affected.

first_step: Send a short erratum note to the authors of arXiv 2308.02342 and 2504.00987, and edit Wikipedia 'Littlewood polynomial'. Suggested replacement text: 'Golay's 12.32 is a heuristic prediction for typical long sequences; the optimal merit factor is now known (OpenAI 2026, Lean-checked) to be unbounded as N->inf, with no effective rate; at all lengths of practical interest the best known values are ~9.5 (N<=225) declining to ~6.3-7.8 for N in 300-1000.'
measurement: Revised arXiv versions or new papers that stop citing 12.32 as the limit. A finite-N claim needing retraction would count as a failure of this framing, and none is expected.
risks: Overcorrection is the main risk: authors may wrongly read the result as 'large merit factors are findable'. The proof gives no N0 and no algorithm, and with the explicit constants it needs delta below 1e-15 just to certify F>6.34. A secondary risk is that the preprint is not peer-reviewed, although the Lean check covers the statement.

title: Use the 076 relax-and-round pipeline as a seed generator for LABS heuristics
summary: A finite analogue of the 076 construction was tested as tabu-search seeds at N in {101,257,509,1021,2053,4099}, 3 runs each at a fixed budget: a sampled quadratic-phase (chirp) waveform in [-1,1]^N on H blocks with exactly packed sweep intervals, then sign or greedy-L4 rounding. It beats random seeds at every N (+0.1 to +0.6 after search). It slightly beats Legendre at N=101 (6.17-6.24 vs 5.84-6.03, inconclusive), but loses clearly to rotated/appended Legendre seeds at every N>=257 (e.g. 4.97-5.10 vs 6.33 at N=1021; 4.52-4.74 vs 6.34 at N=4099). The proof's real auxiliary polynomial needs ~8/delta torus variables with doubly exponential Fourier support, so it cannot be instantiated.

measurement: Best merit factor at a fixed TS budget versus Legendre-seeded runs at N in {509,1021,2053,4099}, at least 3 seeds each.
risks: Confirmed in our small runs: the finite analogue is far below the classical algebraic seed. Our analogue simplified the construction (F=cos, a single mode) and the rounding (greedy, not Lovett-Meka), so it does not refute the pipeline in principle. However, the paper's own constants (rounding C=196608 in Lean, delta<1e-15 to beat 6.34) show the faithful version is useless at any feasible N.

title: Expect better binary radar/CDMA codes or quantum-advantage implications from unbounded merit factor
summary: The result is existential with no rate: N0(eta) is unspecified. The paper and the Lean doc both state that there is no useful convergence rate and no efficient signing algorithm. Practical code design uses N<=~10^4, where records are ~9.5 (N<=225), ~7-8 (N 300-530), ~6.3-6.4 (N~1000+), and practice already prefers PSL-optimized codes, mismatched filters or polyphase codes. Quantum LABS benchmarks are at N<=~40-100, where exact optima (N<=66) are what matters.

title: Binary OFDM PMEPR -> 1 via ultraflat Littlewood polynomials
summary: For one BPSK-OFDM symbol with N subcarriers, the continuous-time PMEPR equals max|P|^2/N. Theorem 1.1 of the 076 papers therefore says the PMEPR infimum over binary words tends to 1, versus 2 for Rudin-Shapiro/Golay complementary codewords (our check: PR-Shapiro 2.00, best Legendre rotation 2.4-2.7, random 6.5-9.3 at N=256-4096). The result does not help a real channel. A single fixed data-free word has zero information rate, and real systems carry data, where Schmidt's covering-radius bound and coding constraints dominate. 5G NR uses pi/2-BPSK with DFT-s-OFDM plus FDSS rather than OFDM codeword selection, and the construction is non-effective anyway.

title: Stop computational searches for circulant Hadamard orders / even Barker lengths (Logan-Mossinghoff-style)
summary: Number-theoretic sieves (Wieferich-pair conditions, field descent) had reduced the problem to 4,489 candidate orders up to 4e30, plus the single surviving Barker candidate n~3.98e33. These are now moot. This matters to a handful of researchers and should be recorded in formal-conjectures, where the Barker statement is still tagged open while the circulant statement is tagged solved.
